text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU autoscaler errors in us-west-2. Queue growth > 95th percentile for 18m. Throttling observed. Paging oncall. alert_id=autoscale_gpu_1768504321

ana (oncall): I’m on it. Looking at metrics now — can someone post the autoscaler logs?

raj (eng-runtime): I have a quick snapshot. Seeing repeated failures to bind pods due to 'no suitable GPU memory slice' from the scheduler. Suspect MIG fragmentation + binpacking issue. Past hour: 14 nodes reporting partially-allocated GPUs.

marta (eng-sre): Confirmed. queue_length: 13k -> 28k in 20m. Throttle rate jumped to 42%. Error spikes coincide with batch allocation failures.

ana (oncall): ops-bot, dump node/gpu allocation table and recent autoscaler events.

ops-bot: Command executed: `rbx infra list-gpu-alloc --region us-west-2 --since 20m`

```
Node   GPU_alloc   MIG_layout  free_slices
node-a 1/4         1x1g+1x2g    0
node-b 2/4         4x1g        0
node-c 0/4         2x2g        2
node-d 3/4         1x1g+1x2g    0
node-e 0/4         1x4g        1
```

ops-bot: Autoscaler events: `scale_up` attempted x3, rejected due to 'instance quota' or 'exceeded group size' on each attempt.

ana (oncall): Ugh. So we have stranded capacity due to mixed MIG sizes and quota/scale limits preventing more nodes. Can we force rebalance?

raj (eng-runtime): Two short-term options: 1) Reconfigure autoscaler max-to-limit to allow burst (needs approvals), or 2) Reduce model footprint / fall back to smaller model variants and route some traffic to other regions. Repacking nodes (recreate) to consistent MIG would fix fragmentation but takes ~10-15m per node and causes drains.

marta (eng-sre): For immediate relief, reduce max_concurrency and batch size at the router to lower per-request allocation. That will reduce allocation pressure while we do heavier fixes.

ana (oncall): Do it. Reduce batch_size from 32->8 and max_concurrency from 64->16 for affected model routes. sam, can you apply?

sam (infra): Applying policy change now. Pushing config to router (canary first).

```
kubectl apply -f /ops/router/overrides/us-west-2-burst-lower-batch.yaml
```

sam (infra): Canary done. No errors. Rolling to 10% traffic.

marta (eng-sre): Monitoring queue. Initial drop from 28k -> 22k in 5m. Throttling down to 31%. Small win.

olivia (support): Starting customer impact message draft for customers in us-west-2. Should we say degraded performance and queued requests? Toni, want to align on wording?

toni (customer-success): Yes. Keep it factual: impacted requests may see increased latency or transient failures; engineers are actively mitigating; expected improved routing within 30–60m.

olivia (support): Draft posted: "Hi — we are investigating increased latency and throttling for inference in us-west-2. Engineers are applying mitigations; expected partial relief in ~30m. We'll follow up with a full postmortem." Please review.

ana (oncall): Thanks. Back to technical. We still have autoscaler failing due to instance pool hitting max size. What's current pool config? raj?

raj (eng-runtime): Instance group `gpu-pool-usw2` max=120, desired=120, quota for account permits 120, but nodes are fragmented with mixed MIG profiles (1g,2g,4g). Autoscaler tries to add a 4g node but pending pod needs 1g slices due to binpacking policy, scheduler can't fit pod on new 4g node because affinity rules prefer matching MIG layouts -> scale rejected.

marta (eng-sre): Also seeing AWS AZ-level limits — one AZ is at vCPU limit so new instances are failing intermittently. That caused 3 scale_up attempts to timeout and roll back.

ana (oncall): Options: 1) Temporarily change scheduler to ignore MIG-layout affinity to allow placement on new nodes (fast but risks degrading packing efficiency). 2) Force a resize of some nodes to smaller MIG partitioning (requires node reboot). 3) Move traffic to other regions. Which is safest fast fix?

raj (eng-runtime): I can flip the scheduler flag now to relax MIG affinity for 10m. That should let pending pods land on new nodes we can spin up. But we still need to get autoscaler to actually create nodes — need AZ quota workaround.

sam (infra): I can request an emergency quota bump in the cloud console, but that takes 5-20m to approve. Meanwhile we can try launching spot instances in different AZs as a stopgap.

ana (oncall): Do both. Raj flip the affinity relax. Sam, spin spot launchers in other AZs. Marta watch for regressions.

raj (eng-runtime): Done. Flipped `scheduler.features.allow_mig_affinity_relax=true` (can revert).

sam (infra): Launching spot requests in az-b and az-c. Using instance type g5. Waiting on allocations.

ops-bot: New nodes detected: node-x1 (az-b) node-x2 (az-c). GPU drivers OK.

marta (eng-sre): Autoscaler now created 2 nodes via spot. Pending pod backlog dropped from 22k -> 9k in 12m. Throttle down to 14%.

olivia (support): Updating customers: added note that we've enabled temporary routing + reduced batch sizes; partial relief observed.

toni (customer-success): Good. Highlight that we may need a longer maintenance to rebalance MIGs and that we'll provide a timeline.

ana (oncall): Next: plan for durable fix — we should schedule a rolling re-provision to unify MIG sizes (move to uniform 1g slices) to avoid future fragmentation. Estimate: 6-8 nodes/hour, 2–3 hours total if staggered. Need change window and approvals.

raj (eng-runtime): Agree. Also propose autoscaler improvement: prefer node flavors that produce required slice sizes or allow binpacking override when existing capacity is fragmented. I'll open a ticket.

marta (eng-sre): I'll start a runbook for manual rebalance steps (drain node, reprovision MIG layout, rejoin). Will include safe drain thresholds and how to avoid mass cache eviction.

kevin (oncall-2): Quick heads-up — I’ll take over from ana at 1768504800 (20m in). Ana, anything outstanding for handoff?

ana (oncall): Handoff: mitigations applied (batch downscale, scheduler relax, spot nodes launched). Customers notified. Remaining: confirm quota bump, start reprovision schedule, postmortem. Watch queue for re-accumulation.

kevin (oncall-2): Got it. I’m monitoring panels now.

olivia (support): Customer communications sent to 14 accounts flagged with errors. No major enterprise customers flagged yet, but one mid-market account reported a 503 spike — support case #15432 opened.

toni (customer-success): We'll proactively reach out to the 3 high-volume customers inside the region.

anna (typo): (small note) maybe keep node reprovision to off-peak hours for lower impact.

marta (eng-sre): Agreed. Will propose a window at 03:00 UTC.

raj (eng-runtime): Created ticket INF-9123: "Fix MIG fragmentation & autoscaler binpack policy" with immediate action items.

ops-bot: Incident status: Mitigated. Root cause: MIG fragmentation + AZ/quota limits prevented autoscaler scale_up -> queue growth & throttling. Next steps: schedule reprovision, autoscaler policy changes, postmortem.

kevin (oncall-2): Marking incident as MONITORED. Will keep thread open until reprovision scheduled.

olivia (support): Final customer update sent: engineers confirm partial mitigation; further maintenance planned with advance notice.

kevin (oncall-2): Closing handoff. If queue > 10k or throttle > 30% ping this thread and @raj.

-- thread end --
